findings.description: storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS MySQL instance's underlying storage, snapshots and automated backups unencrypted, so any exposure of the volumes or snapshots discloses data in cleartext.

publicly_accessible = true gives the database an internet-routable endpoint (also published via the db_endpoint output), exposing the MySQL service and its predictable 'admin' account to internet-wide credential attacks; this is compounded by the database being unencrypted at rest.

The master username is hard-coded to the predictable value 'admin' and the password is passed through a plain Terraform variable, which is persisted in cleartext in Terraform state and re-used in EC2 user data instead of being sourced from Secrets Manager or a managed master password.

The RDS master username and plaintext password (var.password) are interpolated into the user_data script and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc; EC2 user data is retrievable through the instance metadata service (including via SSRF in the hosted PHP app) or ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking database credentials.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled; an SSRF or code-execution flaw in the deployed PHP application can retrieve the highly privileged instance profile credentials and the secret-bearing user data.
No root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance volume that stores the plaintext database credential file dbinfo.inc may be unencrypted at rest.

The bootstrap script installs only httpd serving plain HTTP; the deployed form submits user-supplied data (and the app's DB session traffic) without TLS, allowing interception of data in transit on an internet-facing host.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the instance profile of an internet-facing web server, so theft of instance credentials (readily achievable via IMDSv1/SSRF) yields full control of all S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS databases in the account, including privilege escalation via ec2/iam-adjacent actions.
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, giving a compromised database tier an unconstrained outbound path for data exfiltration or command-and-control.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced for DB connections
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the publicly accessible database accepts plaintext client connections, permitting interception of credentials and query data in transit.
